boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places for studying, meeting, creating, exercising, attending programs, and taking a deliberate break between classes.

cards.title: Choose Your Own Study Volume
cards.subtitle: Quiet and collaborative zones under one roof
cards.notes: Match the room to the task: use a quiet area for focused reading or reserve a tech-enabled study room when your group needs to talk.
cards.short_summary: A flexible academic base for solo work, research help, and collaborative sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC says Bishop Library provides collaborative and quiet study spaces as well as technology-enabled classrooms, conference rooms, and study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Library access and room availability follow current library schedules and policies; check the official library page before visiting.

cards.title: Study Beside the Fireplace
cards.subtitle: An informal upper-level room inside Mund
cards.notes: Bring reading or meet one classmate here when you want a softer setting than a classroom; leave reservable group work to designated rooms.
cards.short_summary: Mund’s fireplace living room supports informal studying and low-key conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC identifies the Wengert Living Room with fireplace on Mund College Center’s upper level and describes it as a place to study.
cards.access_notes: Located on the upper level of Mund College Center; building access is subject to campus operations and posted restrictions.

cards.title: Reset Between Commuter Classes
cards.subtitle: A lower-level Mund space for commuting students
cards.notes: Use the microwave and refrigerator for a packed meal, then study or relax between classes without making another trip away from campus.
cards.short_summary: A practical between-class base designed specifically around commuter needs.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC states that the Commuter Lounge is for commuting students to study, eat, and relax and includes vending, gaming systems, a microwave, refrigerator, and television.
cards.access_notes: Located on Mund College Center’s lower level and intended for commuting students; follow current building-access rules.

cards.title: Look Below Mund for Campus Programs
cards.subtitle: A multi-use lounge and event room
cards.notes: Check the campus events listing before heading downstairs; the room shifts between talks, workshops, performances, and student programs.
cards.short_summary: A flexible lower-level venue whose setup changes with the campus calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC lists The Underground on Mund’s lower level and describes it as a multi-use space with a lounge area and seating for up to 50 in lecture style.
cards.source_title: Conference & Event Services - Lebanon Valley College
cards.access_notes: Attend scheduled programs or use the space as permitted; student groups must arrange room reservations through Conference Services.

cards.title: Pause by the Peace Garden Pond
cards.subtitle: An outdoor setting tied to new-student orientation
cards.notes: Take a quiet circuit around the pond between commitments, and keep the area clear when orientation’s Water Ceremony is underway.
cards.short_summary: A reflective outdoor stop that also carries a documented role in welcoming new students.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC’s 2026 orientation schedule places its self-led Water Ceremony in the Peace Garden, where families bring water from home to symbolize the transition to a new home.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation - Admission and Financial Aid
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may be affected by weather or scheduled campus programs; orientation activities are intended for participating students and families.

cards.title: Use the Quad as an Open-Air Meeting Point
cards.subtitle: A south-campus lawn used for gatherings
cards.notes: Pick a visible landmark before meeting your group, then use the open lawn for a brief check-in, outdoor reading, or a scheduled activity.
cards.short_summary: An adaptable lawn for small meetups as well as organized campus gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes the Academic Quad as an open outdoor space for breakout areas and group activities, and its 2026 orientation schedule includes breakfast there.
cards.source_title: Conference & Event Services - Lebanon Valley College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is subject to weather and scheduled events; organized use may require coordination with Conference Services.

cards.title: Find the Campus-Wide Gathering Lawn
cards.subtitle: A south-campus space for outdoor programs
cards.notes: Watch the student calendar for quad programming, or use the lawn between events for an informal meetup that does not obstruct setup areas.
cards.short_summary: A shared green where casual use overlaps with large student-life programs.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes the Social Quad as an open outdoor space for group activities, and the 2026 orientation schedule places outdoor movies, games, and social events there.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation - Admission and Financial Aid
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may change for weather, event setup, or reserved programming; follow posted directions during campus events.

cards.title: Build a Workout Around Open Hours
cards.subtitle: Indoor recreation for the LVC community
cards.notes: Check the current schedule first, bring your LVC ID, and choose among the available track, fitness, pool, or performance spaces.
cards.short_summary: A student wellness hub with several forms of indoor recreation in one complex.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC says the Sports Center supports student recreation and fitness and lists an indoor track, fitness room, pool, and sports performance center among its facilities.
cards.access_notes: Current schedules vary by facility and season. LVC students must check in at the west desk with an LVC ID card.

cards.title: Trade a Study Break for One Exhibition
cards.subtitle: A free gallery in a converted church
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition and semester hours, then give one artwork a focused look instead of trying to rush through the whole show.
cards.short_summary: A compact cultural pause with changing museum and collector loans near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC says the gallery occupies a Gothic Revival former church, hosts five to six exhibitions annually, and offers free admission.
cards.source_title: The Suzanne H. Arnold Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: The gallery is closed for summer 2026 and is scheduled to reopen August 28; consult the official page for semester hours before visiting.

cards.title: See What Is Scheduled Behind the Theater Doors
cards.subtitle: Mund’s venue for films, talks, and productions
cards.notes: Scan the events calendar for a film, lecture, meeting, or theater production; room use outside scheduled programs requires a reservation.
cards.short_summary: A campus room that moves between performance, presentation, and community uses.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC identifies Leedy Theater in Mund College Center as a venue used for movies, meetings, theater productions, lectures, and other group activities.
cards.access_notes: Enter for scheduled events or approved activities; students and groups must submit room-reservation requests through Conference Services.
